packet.title: Why the sky is blue
sentences: Sunlight contains every colour of visible light.
Nitrogen and oxygen molecules are much smaller than a wavelength of light.
Particles that small scatter short wavelengths far more strongly than long ones.
Blue light is scattered several times more than red light.
Violet scatters even more, but the sun emits less of it and human eyes are less sensitive to it.
At sunset sunlight passes through much more air, so most blue is scattered away and red and orange remain.

packet.title: The physicist who explained the sky
sentences: Lord Rayleigh published the theory of light scattering by small particles in 1871.
